correctness.rationale: The impulse response h_n is the exact n-reservoir Gamma/Erlang kernel. For n=4 the derivative after the second input is an explicitly given cubic; its discriminant factors as -27 exp(s) s² F(s). The Vieta sign test decides whether three real cubic roots are all positive, and the strict monotonicity of G=exp(-s) F gives exactly one transition in (2,3). The s=3 and s>3, and n=2,3, cases were separately established including double-root and transition boundaries. The finite-width persistence argument is local uniform convergence of discharge derivatives near simple roots, not numerical extrapolation. The included program reruns 1500 coefficient and 1500 discriminant checks, supporting but not replacing proof.

value.rationale: A rain routing cascade can merge two hydrograph peaks into one even for separate storms. For the first nontrivial stage depth, this result identifies the exact smallest dimensionless separation needed to resolve two peaks, showing resolution below the individual impulse time-to-peak and persistence for small finite-width storm pulses. This quantitatively motivated sharp physical boundary is not a routine parameter normalization or unexplained narrow numerical constant.
